finding: §6.2/§6.3 (and §1) extend --harness-note and harness_stale symmetrically to the audit loop, so an orchestrator can carry standing judgement-shaping framing for an audit sub-agent too. But §6.4's 'judgement-shaping text belongs in roles, not the wrapper' guidance names only the review role homes (`tp.review_roles` frontmatter and `.tp/reviewers/*.json`). The sanctioned homes for audit-role judgement framing — `tp.audit_roles` focus overrides and `.tp/auditors/*.json` — are never named, leaving the audit half of the newly-symmetric harness feature without a stated 'where it belongs instead' target.
suggestion: In §6.4, name the audit-side sanctioned homes alongside the review ones (e.g. '`tp.review_roles`/`tp.audit_roles` frontmatter and `.tp/reviewers/*.json`/`.tp/auditors/*.json`, all recorded via `roles_hash`'), so the 'belongs in roles' guidance covers both loops the harness note applies to.

finding: Branch 3 fires when 'a mechanize_candidates class present, none blocking'. §8.2 (modified this round) newly claims branch 3 is 'reachable on both --status and --record' because '--status derives the array from the recorded rounds the same way' — a finding class 'that recurs across rounds'. The recurrence threshold (how many recorded rounds a class must appear in before it populates mechanize_candidates) is never pinned in the spec. Test 14 requires asserting that a round with mechanize_candidates present names the compound branch-3 directive, but without the threshold two engineers build different recorded-state fixtures (a class in 2 rounds vs 3 rounds) and disagree on whether next_action resolves to branch 3 or falls through to branch 4 — a non-deterministic test.
suggestion: State the exact recurrence count that populates mechanize_candidates (e.g. a class appearing in ≥N of the recorded rounds), and that --status and --record apply the identical count, so branch-3 reachability and Test 14's branch-3 fixture are deterministically constructible.

finding: §8.4's closing sentence — 'The same --compact stripping applies to the audit --status/--record equivalents' — and Test 18 ('retaining next_action and nonblocking_open; accepted_open is not emitted; the same holds for tp audit --status --compact') read as asserting that audit --compact retains nonblocking_open. But audit convergence is purely status-based (§4.4) and nonblocking_open is a review-severity field emitted only on a clean review round with surviving non-blocking findings (§4.2); audit never emits it. An engineer cannot write a deterministic assertion for the audit --compact case: is nonblocking_open expected-absent-always, or expected-retained-when-present? The two clauses are testably ambiguous for audit.
suggestion: Scope the audit sentence: for audit --status/--record --compact only harness_note and harness_stale are stripped and next_action is retained; state that nonblocking_open is not an audit field at all (never emitted regardless of --compact), so Test 18's audit clause asserts its permanent absence, not its retention.

finding: Test 18 reads '…omit harness_note and harness_stale while retaining next_action and nonblocking_open; … the same holds for tp audit --status --compact'. But nonblocking_open is a review-only field: §4.2 emits it only from the severity-aware review convergence path, and §4.4/§8/§10.4 keep audit convergence status-based with no non-blocking notion. So the audit clause ('the same holds') asserts audit retains nonblocking_open under --compact, a field audit never emits — untestable and misleading. §8.4's matching phrase 'keeping review and audit compaction symmetric' overclaims the same way (nonblocking_open is asymmetric).
suggestion: Scope the audit clause to the fields audit actually emits: in Test 18 say the audit equivalents omit harness_note/harness_stale and retain next_action (nonblocking_open being review-only); and in §8.4 qualify 'symmetric' to the harness/next_action stripping, noting nonblocking_open exists only on the review side.
